overall: Board of Assessors did not violate the Open Meeting Law on the abatement-in-executive-session claim; the minutes request was left open, with the Board directed to review the minutes within 30 days.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board refuses to consider real estate abatement applications in a public meeting and considers them only in executive session.
allegations.key_passage: discuss and vote on applications for tax abatement or exemption.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board refused a written request to inspect and copy non-exempt executive session minutes from its February and March 2012 meetings.
allegations.key_passage: If it has not already done so, the Board should undertake a review in accordance with this guidance within thirty (30) days of receipt of this letter to determine whether publication of the minutes

allegations.summary: Town Counsel asked whether a request for executive session minutes should be read to include documents used at the corresponding meeting; the AG answered this guidance question.
allegations.key_passage: in the absence of a specific request for such documents, a request for minutes need not be construed as including a request for all documents and exhibits used at the corresponding meeting.

remedy: Within thirty (30) days of receipt of the letter, if not already done, the Board should review under the AG's FAQ guidance whether publication of its February 7, 2012 and March 2012 executive session minutes, in whole or in part, may defeat the lawful purposes of those sessions.
